stack slots exact (spill order = declaration order), cross-jump stubs, fold/range spellings, D_800A38DC switch (case 3 first), u16 state local, abs form, per-region temps; candidate.c

R1/R2 register-exact (447/449/445 statement order, table-loop state var split from st, 0xF-case value split); nav leg loop kept a C while loop (reorg fills its delay slot from the loop head only with a LOOP_BEG note); random-pick `score` is its own local (ablation: best of 11 single-role splits)

role ablation minimised sharing (tired/near/wtype/cnt/ok4/far/lim/besti split at no cost; every remaining shared role is load-bearing); flip is an s8 sharing a local with the D_80099D88+6 byte (tired) so it seats s1 ahead of score

frontier.hypothesis: BLOCKER (needs owner ruling): the three jump tables cannot be placed byte-exactly by the current pipeline even after TU re-attribution.
frontier.mechanism: target tables sit at 0x8001585C/84/9C (all 4 mod 8) with one zero word after table 1 and table 2 - the original assembler's .align 3 applied relative to the object. Our pipeline seds .align 3 -> .align 2 for text1b (Makefile RODATA_ALIGN2_FILES), which drops the gaps; GNU as .align 3 is absolute, so no text1b.o(.rodata) placement can put table 1 at a 4-mod-8 address. The project's existing workaround (an explicit const zero word between functions, e.g. D_800159CC) cannot reach gaps between three tables emitted back to back by one function.
frontier.next_probe: owner decision: (a) pipeline emulation of object-relative .align 3 for rodata (maspsx/sed pass emitting explicit padding; touches every RODATA_ALIGN2 file and the existing zero-word consts), or (b) another sanctioned route. Only then move 0x8001585C..0x80015988 from src/text1a_b_pre_rodata.c into src/text1b.c at the right source positions.

frontier.hypothesis: lh+sra 4 for (0x438 >> 4) at 0x8005AB34 and 0x8005ACCC needs a spelling where combine cannot merge the sign-extending load with the shift.
